title: Establish synthetic Fleet/provider performance baseline
source_ranges: fleet_architecture_spec_v0_3.md §9.2 lines 651-675; §37.1 lines 2249-2254; §46 R-SEC-01 lines 2533-2539; §48.1 lines 2639-2644 and §48.2 V3-S11 line 2665
body:
## Why / user outcome
Establish a repeatable synthetic benchmark before selecting cache/provider changes or claiming BWS latency is intrinsic. Produce a reproducible baseline covering Fleet's current resolver/broker and comparable provider paths, with no production secret access.

## Current evidence and affected code
Baseline commit `34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e` (2026-11-12): `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs` implements broker transport then BWS CLI list/get fallback; `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/secrets_broker.rs` refreshes via BWS CLI, list plus per-secret get at bounded concurrency; `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/secrets.rs` has only `get` and `list`. No benchmark command or Fleet provider SDK dependency is present. No performance timings have been measured. V1 describes this current-state census only; this proposal is V2-foundation.

## Deliverable and technical boundaries
Add an opt-in benchmark harness and report. Start with deterministic fake/in-process sources. Provider comparisons may include broker, direct BWS CLI, official BWS Rust SDK only after SDK parity/MSRV verification, `op` CLI, fnox CLI and published `fnox-client`, local SOPS/age decrypt, and separately authorized `bw` CLI. Keep BWS, OP and BW identities/scopes distinct. Live access, if separately authorized, is restricted to disposable isolated fixture vaults/projects. No personal/production vault reads or writes, no changes to current resolver behavior, no secret-bearing stderr/value output.

## Measurable acceptance and oracle
1. Matrix records cold/warm process and auth; sequential and batch 1/10/100/1000 records (also 500 as intermediate); concurrency curves; batch where provider supports it; first/full paginated list/full census; cache hit/miss; synthetic create/update/readback only in disposable store; auth overhead; throttles/failures/recovery.
2. Report sample count, p50/p95/p99, quantile confidence intervals, throughput, error/timeout/throttle rate, bytes, CPU, peak/RSS memory, process count/startup, token/session churn, provider/cache age, exact versions, host/OS and RTT. Separate network, auth/startup, provider, serialization and cache latency where observable. Cover laptop and actual agent host if available; include low-concurrency 24-hour soak before systemic slowness claims. Define p99 as nearest-rank `x_(ceil(0.99 n))` over successful completed-operation latencies; `x_(i)` is the one-based i-th sorted value, retaining ties (never jitter). For IID/stationary trials, compute a two-sided equal-tail, at-least-95%-coverage nonparametric order-statistic interval: let `B~Binomial(n,0.99)`; choose the largest lower rank `k` with `P(B<k)<=0.025` and smallest upper rank `l` with `P(B>=l)<=0.025`; report `[x_(k),x_(l)]`, n, k/l, endpoints and quantile convention. Equal endpoints from ties are reported as observed. A 100-sample cell is exploratory, not reliable p99; the ≥10,000-operation floor alone does not establish interval precision. If dependence, nonstationarity or censoring invalidates IID, label p99 exploratory/unavailable or preregister a block-bootstrap method and block-length rule before seeing outcomes; never choose post hoc. Report interval width; wide/unavailable intervals cannot support superiority. Retain all attempts and report failures, timeouts and throttles separately; timed-out/censored attempts are not silently dropped.
3. Provide repeatable command and raw anonymized timings. Do not invent target values before baseline. Oracle: deterministic scripted-provider event trace validates labels/failures; independently recompute nearest-rank quantile and exact-binomial CI from sorted retained samples, including rank indices and tied endpoints. Randomized/interleaved design supports IID assumption; otherwise p99 is exploratory unless block bootstrap and block-length rule are preregistered. No benchmark was run in this design phase.
4. Synthetic canary value is absent from stdout/stderr, JSON, logs, telemetry, panic/crash output and artifacts.

## Negative tests
403/permission denial, 429/Retry-After, timeout, malformed/truncated pagination, provider absence, unsupported SDK, empty result and read-after-write mismatch remain distinct and never imply deletion. No live credentials configured by default. Harness refuses production-designated scopes.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
No implementation dependency; optional real provider runs require capability verification plus explicit isolated-vault authorization. High priority, urgency 450, medium size, V2-foundation, Ready as synthetic work.

## Rollback / recovery
Opt-in command and adapters only; disable/remove benchmark paths without changing `get/list`. No provider mutation outside disposable approved fixture and no persisted secret values.

## Open decision
After baseline, implementation owner proposes p95/p99 and regression budgets with workload rationale; reviewers can refine, without waiting on user-supplied thresholds or blocking the benchmark deliverable. Until then, oracle is sound reproducible measurement, not threshold attainment.



## Priority, lifecycle and sizing
Intrinsic urgency 450 (High); queue projection 20 only if the existing queue field is populated (High→20, Standard→40, Low/Someday/Cold→70). This intrinsic score is not the queue score and is separate from importance, dependencies, lifecycle and dispatch. Size M; lifecycle Ready; stage V2-foundation; lane OpenCode implementation/test.
security_classification: Synthetic benchmark fixtures; no production credential classification.

title: Define and enforce canonical per-secret freshness policy
body:
## Why / user outcome
Define one canonical, policy-owned per-secret freshness contract so cache age, provider outage, rotation and revocation cannot be confused. This proposal is the owner of freshness semantics for #9160. Related architecture, broker and reconciliation packets consume this contract; they must not invent competing max-age defaults or duplicate its policy model.

## Current evidence and affected code
`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs` is an uncached redacted broker/BWS resolver. Broker code `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/secrets_broker.rs` has per-secret installation, fetched timestamps, age/source, singleflight and partial-refresh behavior from merged PR #8491 (`c676d1c41c07`), with reported 59/59 tests. #6767 is still OPEN for deployment verification/live canary. That deployment/canary is not authorized in this run. V1 is current-state census, not a new implementation stage. Do not reimplement PR #8491 or claim deployed proof.

## Deliverable and technical boundaries
Specify and implement only the missing policy semantics over existing source age/provenance: cache/result states, typed max-age decision, `refresh-required`/`stale` outcomes, unavailable/inaccessible/not-found distinction, revocation precedence, and class-specific stale/offline eligibility. Preserve exact provider/account/project/vault/profile scope. Ordinary resolver/hot cache/snapshot must categorically exclude root private-key bytes, including a nominal `live-only` cache; a separately authorized bounded in-memory signer operation and encrypted root escrow are separate custody interfaces. Do not add a persistent cache, new provider, reconciliation writer, or silent legacy CLI change.

## API and behavior
Result carries source/native reference, observed revision if available, fetched-at/age, authority/cache state, class and freshness decision without revealing values. Policy chooses live-only, bounded-stale or snapshot-eligible per class; provider 403, timeout, incomplete list and unknown revocation never become absence/deletion. Successful Fleet-mediated writes must invalidate exact ordinary secret identity before reporting success; where no write path currently exists, specify contract for later consumer rather than inventing one here. Stale/snapshot data never authorizes writes or updates a provider.

## Measurable acceptance and oracle
1. A model-based test generator exercises fresh/expired age, live-only and bounded-stale classes, revocation, scoped aliases, outage/403, incomplete listing, refresh failure/success and recovery using fake clock/provider.
2. Invariants: failed refresh never advances fetched-at; age over declared maximum is denied; revocation deny wins over warm entry; 403/outage/partial inventory never means deleted; same-name secrets in distinct scopes do not alias; allowed stale responses are marked and bounded; ordinary secret write invalidation is exact and synchronous where a write API exists.
3. Existing #8491 behavior/tests are reused; add tests only for policy decisions not already covered. Existing #6767 deployment/canary remains separate; do not run canary.
4. Oracle is a versioned reference state model compared after every generated operation with fake-clock/provider traces; redaction scanner proves values absent from Debug/errors/logs/status.
5. Implementation owner derives proposed per-class initial age defaults from PERF-01 measurements plus risk rationale and records them in the reviewable policy/report. This proposal can be reviewed/refined without blocking or awaiting a user-picked numeric threshold; tests use explicit policy fixtures, not magic production timing.

## Negative tests
Over-age but otherwise valid value, revoked value, unknown age, backward clock, 403-as-absence, truncated inventory, stale divergent replica, failed refresh, same-name cross-scope collision, and cache result used as write authority all fail closed as policy requires. Root private-key bytes cannot enter or be returned by ordinary resolver/cache/snapshot tests. Live canary is expressly not an acceptance criterion.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Reuses #6767 and merged PR #8491 as implementation baseline. High priority, urgency 450, medium size, V2-foundation, Ready for synthetic/model work. Consumers are `designs/secrets.md` and `designs/reconciliation.md`; active implementation consumers are ARCH-01, SEC-03 and REC-07. They consume PERF-02’s canonical semantics and must not duplicate its policy or define competing age defaults.

## Rollback / recovery
Version policy/result behavior; high-risk classes fail closed if policy absent or malformed. Rollback cannot claim freshness or restore high-risk stale serving. Recover only by authoritative reread and exact invalidation. No live rotation, deployment, provider write, or canary.



## Priority, lifecycle and sizing
Intrinsic urgency 450 (High); queue projection 20 only if the existing queue field is populated (High→20, Standard→40, Low/Someday/Cold→70). This intrinsic score is not the queue score and is separate from importance, dependencies, lifecycle and dispatch. Size M; lifecycle Ready; stage V2-foundation; lane OpenCode implementation/test.
security_classification: Per-secret freshness policy; root private-key bytes excluded from ordinary resolver/cache/snapshot.

title: Evaluate optional fnox daemon read-cache adapter
source_ranges: docs.rs fnox-client 1.48.0 public Client API; fnox daemon/sync/provider official docs; pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml workspace MSRV
body:
## Why / user outcome
Determine with source and measurement whether fnox's public daemon client accelerates a real Fleet consumer without moving freshness, authorization or write policy into a second resolver. Produce go/no-go; no wholesale adoption.

## Current evidence and affected code
Primary docs.rs `fnox-client` 1.48.0 (published 2026-11-09) expose `Client::new`, `with_timeout`, `hello`, `resolve_env` and `EnvOutcome`; it is read-only, talks to an already-running daemon, and cannot start it, populate it or call providers. fnox docs state daemon is memory-only per-user IPC and explicit refresh/clear is required after rotation. Provider docs show BWS uses CLI and can write via fnox; OP and BW human-vault adapters are read-only. Fleet current resolver is `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets`; workspace MSRV is 1.85 in `pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml`. No compatibility build or performance measurement exists.

## Deliverable and technical boundaries
A bounded synthetic prototype and adoption decision comparing fnox CLI, `fnox exec`, published public `fnox-client` daemon hit, and corrected Fleet path. Use public API only; no private wire protocol. Optional feature only, no mandatory fnox dependency, no env dump/broad injection, provider writes, reconciliation, root-key bytes or signer cache. A daemon hit is not freshness authority; PERF-02 policy wins. On miss/disabled/unavailable use Fleet's authoritative resolver or typed failure. Confirm actual MSRV/dependency/platform compatibility before proposing adoption.

## API and behavior
Only request allow-listed key names needed by the consumer. Map hit/miss/disabled/daemon absent/protocol mismatch/timeout distinctly. Never turn miss into empty/not-found. Never read stale daemon entry where PERF-02 demands live age/revocation. On miss do not rely on fnox-client to trigger provider read; it cannot.

## Measurable acceptance and oracle
1. Pin crate/binary versions and compile/test under Fleet declared MSRV/toolchain; record transitive dependency, feature, platform and startup/RSS effect. If impossible, verified incompatibility is a no-go result, not a blocker to other work.
2. Synthetic tests cover hit, miss, disabled, daemon absent, old protocol, timeout, environment/profile/config mismatch, refresh/clear, malformed result, and fallback mapping. A call trace proves the client did not spawn daemon or fetch providers.
3. Use PERF-01 equivalent-freshness benchmark: p50/p95/p99, memory, startup/process count, errors and stale age. Implementation owner proposes measured improvement target with workload rationale after baseline; reviewers refine without waiting on user or blocking. Adopt only with demonstrated relevant gain, zero stale/revoked violations, supported dependency/platform and kill switch; otherwise record CLI-only/reject.
4. Oracle: known synthetic key-value/version plus instrumented provider/daemon call trace and independent quantile recomputation. No fabricated timings.

## Negative tests
Rotated/revoked value sitting in daemon cannot override PERF-02 deny; stale hit fails for freshness-required class; miss/disabled not-found confusion fails; different environment cannot reuse wrong-profile entry; wrong protocol does not panic; secret canary never enters argv, logs or errors.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends on PERF-01 baseline and PERF-02 canonical freshness semantics. High research priority, intrinsic urgency 600, medium size, V2, Backlog. Synthetic local fixture only; isolated live provider requires separate authorization.

## Rollback / recovery
Optional feature kill switch; fallback retains existing broker/BWS path and PERF-02 rules. Remove integration and optional dependency if no measurable benefit or compatibility. Do not modify deployed daemon, live provider or cache.



## Priority, lifecycle and sizing
Intrinsic urgency 600 (High); queue projection 20 only if the existing queue field is populated (High→20, Standard→40, Low/Someday/Cold→70). This intrinsic score is not the queue score and is separate from importance, dependencies, lifecycle and dispatch. Size M; lifecycle Backlog; stage V2; lane OpenCode research/prototype.
security_classification: Read-only synthetic/test values only; no root/private-key material.

title: Add Fleet-side SOPS/age deployment adapter
source_ranges: fleet_architecture_spec_v0_3.md §§38 lines 2269-2278, 39.1-39.3 lines 2281-2312, 42.2 lines 2386-2389; §48.2 V3-S12 line 2666
note.md lines 32-50; Fleet secrets API surface in pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets and pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/secrets.rs
body:
## Why / user outcome
Provide Fleet's scoped provider/artifact seam for existing SOPS/age ciphertext without reimplementing cryptography or conflating deployment artifacts with remote vault reads. Keep format adapter independently reviewable from NixOS provisioning/recovery (PERF-06).

## Current evidence and affected code
Intake `note.md` lines 32-50 reports SOPS/age patterns already in NixOS configuration, but no Fleet-level SOPS provider. `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets` currently exposes name-based broker/BWS reads; `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/secrets.rs` only get/list. Primary SOPS/age docs support encrypted structured/binary data and recipients. This is not evidence that Fleet can currently provision keys or deploy NixOS secrets.

## Affected code / API
Primary seams: `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs` for an optional source/artifact adapter and `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/secrets.rs` for CLI integration; avoid editing NixOS activation files in this issue. Define a typed scoped SOPS/age adapter with manifest, dry-run, encrypt/decrypt-to-protected-sink and verify operations; exact Rust signatures remain implementation-owned.

## Deliverable and technical boundaries
Add an opt-in Fleet adapter/manifest path that invokes pinned supported SOPS/age tooling or a verified stable library, preserves standard formats, enforces configured scope/recipient policy and produces dry-run/verify receipts. Synthetic values only. Do not implement crypto, NixOS activation or key lifecycle here; PERF-06 handles deployment provisioning/recovery. No automatic export of BWS/OP, root private key, live values, Git plaintext, or secret interpolation into Nix store. Any production export/deployment is Blocked pending explicit scoped approval and separate reviewed custody controls. Root material cannot flow through ordinary resolver/cache.

## API and behavior
Provider API should expose inspect/validate/encrypt/decrypt-to-protected-sink/verify operations with explicit recipient set and metadata-only dry-run. Failure is typed (missing key, invalid ciphertext, unauthorized scope, unsupported format, IO/integrity). No decrypted values in ordinary JSON/status. Exact CLI command syntax remains implementation-owned but must declare paths and parse strictly before side effects.

## Measurable acceptance and oracle
1. Round-trip synthetic structured and binary fixtures with pinned SOPS/age; independently decrypt and compare expected bytes.
2. Dry-run emits only planned paths, scopes and recipient fingerprints/labels, never plaintext. Verify command confirms ciphertext integrity/recipient policy without exposing value.
3. Adversarial fixtures test wrong/missing identity, unauthorized recipient, corrupt/truncated ciphertext, unsupported schema, partial output, symlink/path traversal and write failure.
4. Oracle: independent pinned SOPS/age invocation plus byte-for-byte synthetic golden fixture, manifest validator and redaction scan.

## Negative tests
Secret marker absent from stdout/stderr/logs/JSON/store; invalid recipient or decrypt failure never falls back to plaintext; output symlink/traversal rejected before write; no default root export; unsupported API capability is not reported successful.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends on PERF-02 class/freshness policy; coordinate artifact and recipient manifest with PERF-06. High, intrinsic urgency 600, medium size, V2, Backlog. Synthetic only.

## Rollback / recovery
Optional adapter, no default deployment activation. Preserve prior ciphertext and report; rollback can restore ciphertext only without claiming to revoke access to historical Git copies. No production Nix change or secret migration.



## Priority, lifecycle and sizing
Intrinsic urgency 600 (High); queue projection 20 only if the existing queue field is populated (High→20, Standard→40, Low/Someday/Cold→70). This intrinsic score is not the queue score and is separate from importance, dependencies, lifecycle and dispatch. Size M; lifecycle Backlog; stage V2; lane OpenCode implementation/test.
security_classification: Deployment ciphertext only, synthetic fixtures; root private keys excluded.

title: Complete bounded SecureStore and AEAD-envelope evaluation
source_ranges: docs.rs securestore 0.100.3; neosmart/securestore-rs and neosmart/SecureStore primary project docs
body:
## Why / user outcome
Complete the source-backed SecureStore technical/maintenance evaluation required by addendum §6 and spec §42.2, and determine whether an AEAD-envelope alternative adds value beyond SOPS/age. The evaluation is required; prototype, import/export adapter and adoption remain conditional outcomes, not assumed deliverables.

## Current evidence and affected code
Docs.rs `securestore` 0.100.3 documents a Rust `SecretsManager` API and portable v3 JSON format; upstream protocol docs specify AES-128-CBC, HMAC-SHA1 and PBKDF2-SHA1 (256,000 iterations), with OpenSSL/Rust backend options. This does not establish a practical break, an independent audit, long-term maintenance, safe concurrent update, or Nix integration. Fleet currently has no SecureStore dependency or format.

## Deliverable and technical boundaries
Research exact SecureStore release/source, maintainer/release evidence, dependencies/MSRV, KDF bounds/upgrades, MAC coverage/order, metadata authentication, downgrade/rollback, key custody, format migration, atomic save/multiprocess concurrency, corruption/recovery and cross-language interoperability. Compare with SOPS/age and a plausible modern envelope built from maintained AEAD primitives with explicit versioning and key wrapping/recipient lifecycle. Explain whether SOPS/age already meets the use case and why a separate envelope prototype is unnecessary, or define a disposable synthetic prototype if comparison exposes a material question. Research is mandatory; prototypes use synthetic values only. No production values, Cargo dependency, new canonical format, migration, root archive or cache adoption. SecureStore remains at most a conditional import/export candidate.

## Measurable acceptance and oracle
1. Evidence matrix cites exact source/release for every claim and labels unknowns; independent crypto reviewer evaluates any deployment-use recommendation.
2. If a concrete use case warrants a prototype, cross-implementation synthetic round-trip tests Rust and .NET implementations where practical; tamper each field, wrong key, truncate, downgrade, rollback, concurrent writer and interrupted save.
3. Compare against SOPS/age multi-recipient recovery/rekey, Nix integration, maintenance and rollback, plus the modern AEAD-envelope alternative described above. Either justify no separate prototype because existing SOPS/age covers the need, or define a tightly scoped synthetic prototype and its oracle.
4. Evaluation is complete even if recommendation is “no prototype/no adoption”; adoption/import remains conditional on evidence and independent review. Oracle: cited primary-source matrix, known synthetic bytes where a prototype runs, cross-implementation equality and expected authenticated failure under mutation; no conclusion based on algorithm names alone.

## Negative tests
Wrong key, tampered ciphertext/metadata, unsupported version, rollback, truncated input, resource-exhausting KDF/input, concurrent lost update and backend mismatch fail safely; no fixture value appears in logs. Do not claim practical exploit or safety without evidence.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
No runtime dependency. Standard priority, intrinsic urgency 1000, medium size, required V2 research backlog; prototype/adoption conditional. External security review required before deployment use.

## Rollback / recovery
Prototype disposable; no production footprint. If no-go, remove prototype; any later adoption requires separate format migration, custody and recovery decision.



## Priority, lifecycle and sizing
Intrinsic urgency 1000 (Standard); queue projection 40 only if the existing queue field is populated (High→20, Standard→40, Low/Someday/Cold→70). This intrinsic score is not the queue score and is separate from importance, dependencies, lifecycle and dispatch. Size M; lifecycle Backlog; stage V2; lane OpenCode research/security review.
security_classification: Synthetic format vectors only; no production secret payloads.

title: Verify NixOS provisioning, age recipient lifecycle and offline recovery
source_ranges: note.md lines 32-50; actual NixOS configuration and sops-nix module to be identified by implementation owner
body:
## Why / user outcome
Prove NixOS sops-nix can provision an authorized synthetic deployment secret safely, keep age identities outside Git/Nix store, and recover offline after host loss. This is separate from Fleet's SOPS/age adapter PERF-04.

## Current evidence and affected files
Intake reports sops-nix patterns in current NixOS config, but exact key paths, persistence and activation behavior have not been verified in this assignment. Official sops-nix docs describe activation-time decrypt to protected runtime files with owner/mode; age recipients enable encryption but old Git ciphertext remains decryptable by removed recipients. No production key or deployment is authorized. Inspect the actual NixOS files and owner before proposing changes.

## Affected configuration / API
Inspect existing repository NixOS flake/module and sops-nix configuration first; record exact paths and owners in the test report rather than guessing. Add only an isolated test module/VM fixture and operator recovery procedure; no Fleet library API changes.

## Deliverable and technical boundaries
Create synthetic test fixture/runbook for protected runtime identity bootstrap, activation, host rebuild/loss, independent recovery recipient, recipient add/remove/rekey, overlap and offboarding. Keep identities and plaintext out of Git, derivations/store paths, CI/logs/images. No live config deployment, production key, root private key or live canary; these operations are Blocked pending explicit scoped approval and reviewed rollback/custody controls. Preserve separate root escrow policy; this issue concerns deployment-secret provisioning/recovery, not root custody.

## Measurable acceptance and oracle
1. Disposable NixOS VM activation creates expected runtime file with declared owner/mode atomically.
2. Recursive derivation/store/closure/log/image scan contains neither synthetic plaintext canary nor private identity.
3. Rebuilt/disconnected test host restores explicitly permitted synthetic subset using independent recovery identity without network.
4. Adding recipient and rekey allows new identity for current ciphertext; removed identity fails current ciphertext. Test and document that old Git history may still decrypt; if revocation is required, rotate underlying secret.
5. Oracle: independent pinned SOPS/age decrypt bytes, filesystem metadata assertions, recursive store scan and isolated restore receipt.

## Negative tests
Identity in repository/store path, wrong/missing identity, mode too broad, wrong owner, partial activation, key persistence loss on reboot, unavailable recovery identity and historical ciphertext still decryptable are detected and never represented as successful revocation/recovery.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends on PERF-04 artifact/recipient manifest contract; configuration owner and disposable VM available. High, intrinsic urgency 600, medium size, V2 backlog. Synthetic keys only.

## Rollback / recovery
Run only in disposable host/config first; preserve known-good encrypted fixture. Rollback cannot resurrect a revoked recipient or claim Git history erasure. Stop before production deployment absent separate explicit approval.



## Priority, lifecycle and sizing
Intrinsic urgency 600 (High); queue projection 20 only if the existing queue field is populated (High→20, Standard→40, Low/Someday/Cold→70). This intrinsic score is not the queue score and is separate from importance, dependencies, lifecycle and dispatch. Size M; lifecycle Backlog; stage V2; lane OpenCode test/operations/documentation.
security_classification: Synthetic deployment secrets; no production or root identity.
